sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section recounts the angels' objection to the giving of the Torah to Moshe and the response, and introduces the Midrashic parallel of three angelic disputes.

translations.translation: When Moshe ascended to the heavens, the ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.: "What is a child of woman doing among us?" He said to them: "He has come to receive the Torah"
(on behalf of all of Israel,
and as the teaching states,
"Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Yehoshua, Yehoshua to the Elders, the Elders to the Prophets, and the Prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly,"
and from them to all of Israel until the end of all generations),
they said before Him
(the angels):
"This hidden treasure that is hidden for You... before the world was created, do You seek to give it to flesh and blood?"
"What
is man that You are mindful of him... Bestow Your glory upon the heavens."
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe: "Return an answer to them," etc.,
and the answer that Moshe Rabbeinu gave them was: "Did you descend to Egypt?... Do you have an evil inclination among you?" etc.
And in the Midrash Tehillim on the verse,
it is stated: "In three places the angels argued against the Holy One, blessed be He:
at the creation of man,
at the giving of the Torah, and at the Mishkan."
When the Holy One, blessed be He, sought to create man, they said: "What is man that You are mindful of him,"
and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed them that His wisdom is greater than yours.
When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to give the Torah to Israel, they said: "What is man that You are mindful of him... Bestow Your glory upon the heavens,"
and similarly they argued also when the command was given: "Make for Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell in their midst."
That is to say,
the statement of the Gemara that the angels' claim was at the giving of the Torah
is explained in the Midrash in more detail,
that in three places the angels argued.
And as an introduction,
behold it is written,
"Ten ten per shekel of the holy shekel,"
that the Ten Utterances correspond to the Ten Commandments,
meaning that the Ten Commandments give permanence to the Ten Utterances,
for through the Torah the intention and purpose of the creation of the world is completed,
that the purpose of the creation of the world is to make the world a dwelling place and Sanctuary for Him, blessed be He,
and this intention is completed through the Torah.
And this is that the angels' claim was in three places:
at the time of creation,
at the Mishkan
(the ultimate intention of the creation of the world),
and at the giving of the Torah
(for through the Torah this intention is completed).
